title: Cyclic open units give arbitrary bounded-primary torsion restriction on contractible tests
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime, $X$ an affine scheme [def-weil-affine-spectrum], $f\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$, $W=X[1/f]$ and $j:W\hookrightarrow X$. Use the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. For an abelian group $M$ let $\underline M_Z$ denote its constant abelian sheaf on $Z_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Use ordinary uncompleted derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with $[0]$ denoting placement in degree zero and $R\Gamma$ computed by K-injective resolutions [def-pur-ringed-site-zeroth-hypercohomology]. For $s\geq1$ put $A_{s,X}=(\mathbf Z/\ell^s\mathbf Z)_X$, regarded as a sheaf of modules over itself, and assume the actual derived adjunction unit $A_{s,X}[0]\to Rj_*j^*A_{s,X}[0]$, for the module inverse image $j^*$ and the K-injective total derived functor $Rj_*$ of the module direct image [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], is an isomorphism in the derived category of $A_{s,X}$-module sheaves for every $s\geq1$.

Let $v:V\to X$ be any affine pro-etale object that is weakly contractible [sk-def-pe-weak-contractible]: evaluation on $V$ sends epimorphisms of sheaves of sets on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ to surjections. Put $T=V\times_XW=V[1/v^*f]$. For every $n\geq1$ and every abelian group $M$ with $\ell^nM=0$, including groups of infinite cardinality, the actual restriction map
$$R\Gamma(V,\underline M_V[0])\longrightarrow R\Gamma(T,\underline M_T[0])$$
is an isomorphism in $D(\mathbf{Ab})$. The source is concentrated in degree zero, and in particular $H^q(T,\underline M_T)=0$ for every $q>0$. These are the maps induced by restriction of sections, natural in homomorphisms of $M$, after forgetting the finite coefficient module action where appropriate. Both $V,T$ are affine and hence qcqs. Empty schemes and the identity open are included.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-finite-constant-unit-restriction] with A=ULift(ZMod(ℓ^s)) for every s≥1. This gives invertibility of the actual derived section restriction on every cyclic primary group.

On V, [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-abelian-evaluation-colimits] makes abelian evaluation exact. Its total derived functor on a degree-zero constant sheaf is therefore the same degree-zero evaluated group, so all nonzero homology vanishes. Both evaluations are nonnegative on degree-zero sheaves.

For each nonnegative degree q, compose the natural restriction with homology. The two resulting coefficient functors are additive and preserve filtered colimits: constant sheaves are a left adjoint, and [lem-sfb-proetale-derived-evaluation-continuity] applies at the affine objects V and T. The cyclic components are invertible by step 1. Apply [lem-sfb-bounded-primary-natural-transformation] to the given group M. Thus restriction is invertible on every nonnegative homology. In negative degrees both sides vanish by step 2.

Homology detects isomorphisms in D(Ab), so the actual restriction is invertible. Transport the source nonzero-degree vanishing across its homology isomorphisms to obtain positive target vanishing. The last assertion is precisely naturality of this already defined restriction transformation.

Step 3: sheafification exactness, the ses triangle, R-derived triangulated and the LES give closure under extensions; the T row is short exact since H^1(T,B_1)=0, so the short five lemma applies with no connecting-map compatibility needed. Step 5: finite subgroups form a small directed exhausting system; colim of constant sheaves via sheafification; det-pe-bounded-continuity-sections with a=0 on the qcqs affine V and T; colimits of isos and zeros. Step 6: iso on all H^q, so an iso in D(Ab). Edge cases: M=0; identity open; W empty forces X empty; T empty with V nonempty is excluded by the s=1 unit.
